title: Chapter 3 Quiz 5
description: Comparing values, combining conditions with AND, OR, NOT, and evaluating them.
instructions: Chapter 3: Comparison, logical operators and conditions.
Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: Match each comparison symbol to its meaning.
questions.explanation: These are the comparison operators of the course.

questions.question: What does the operator **<>** mean?
questions.explanation: <> tests that two values are different.

questions.question: (5 > 3) AND (2 > 4) is True.
questions.explanation: AND needs both sides True. 2 > 4 is False, so the whole condition is False.

questions.question: (5 > 3) OR (2 > 4) is True.
questions.explanation: OR needs only one side True. 5 > 3 is True.

questions.question: NOT (3 = 3) is True.
questions.explanation: 3 = 3 is True, and NOT turns True into False.

questions.question: Which condition means 1 ≤ Index ≤ 10?
questions.explanation: Both limits must hold at the same time, so we use AND. With OR, almost any number would pass.

questions.question: Which is a **simple** condition?
questions.explanation: A simple condition has one comparison. The others combine several.

questions.question: Let x = 4 and y = -2. Say whether each condition is True or False.
questions.explanation: x > 0 is True; x <> y is True; AND needs y > 0, which is False; OR is True because x > 0; NOT (x = y) is True.

questions.question: Let x = 0 and y = 0. Say whether each condition is True or False.
questions.explanation: With x = 0 and y = 0: x > 0 is False; x <> y is False; AND is False; OR is False; NOT (x = y) is False because x = y.

questions.question: A condition with AND is True only when {{1}} sides are True. A condition with OR is True when {{2}} one side is True.
questions.explanation: AND is strict (both). OR is flexible (at least one).
